attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

## Summary of Memo Visibility Enforcement Sites

I've thoroughly searched the codebase for memo visibility enforcement. Here are all the distinct locations where memo access control is implemented:

### **API Route Handlers (gRPC/Connect services)**

1. **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`** (Lines 39-68)
   - `checkMemoReadAccess()` - Central authorization function that enforces:
     - Archived memos only visible to creator
     - Private memos only visible to creator or authenticated user
     - Public memos visible to all
   - Used by: `GetMemo()` (line 356), `ListMemoComments()` (via memo_service_comments.go:148)
   - `ListMemos()` (line 178) - Filters memos by visibility based on current user and unauthenticated status

2. **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go`** (Lines 136-285)
   - `ListMemoComments()` - Calls `checkMemoReadAccess()` on parent memo (line 148)
   - Comment visibility filtering via `memoFilter` (line 160) for related comments
   - `CreateMemoComment()` - Visibility check for whether non-creator can comment (line 41)

3. **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go`** (Lines 15-182)
   - `ListMemoReactions()` - Visibility check on memo (lines 30-40)
   - `UpsertMemoReaction()` - Visibility check before allowing reaction (lines 82-85)
   - Both check if Private memo and user is not creator

4. **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go`** (Lines 200-241)
   - `ListMemoAttachments()` - Visibility check (lines 214-225)
   - Enforces: public attachments visible to all, private only to creator

5. **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go`** (Lines 93-147)
   - `ListMemoRelations()` - Uses visibility filter on memo relations (line 111)
   - Filters related memos by current user's access level

6. **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_share_service.go`** (Lines 21-227)
   - `CreateMemoShare()` - Creator-only check (line 43)
   - `ListMemoShares()` - Creator-only check (line 92)
   - `DeleteMemoShare()` - Creator-only check (line 133)
   - `GetMemoByShare()` - Share token access (no user auth required for valid token)

### **File Server (Attachment Downloads)**

7. **`/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`** (Lines 649-704)
   - `checkAttachmentPermission()` - Enforces visibility for attachment downloads:
     - Unlinked attachments: creator-only
     - Linked to memo: checks memo visibility (Public, Protected, Private)
     - Supports share token fallback access
     - Public attachments require `AllowAnonymous()` profile setting

### **User Stats/Activity Aggregation**

8. **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go`** (Lines 56-250)
   - `ListAllUserStats()` - Visibility filtering (lines 84, 87, 90)
   - `GetUserStats()` - Visibility filtering based on current user (lines 218, 220)
   - Only includes public/protected memos visible to requester

### **Frontend/SEO Endpoints**

9. **`/bench/repo/server/router/frontend/frontend.go`** (Lines 143-166)
   - `getSitemapXML()` - Only includes public memos in sitemap (line 150)

### **RSS Feed Generation**

10. **`/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go`** (Lines 72-160)
    - `GetExploreRSS()` - Public memos only (line 90)
    - `GetUserRSS()` - Public memos only for specific user (line 141)

### **Helper Functions/Utilities**

11. **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/common.go`** (Lines 77-83)
    - `isSuperUser()` - Admin privilege check
    - `canModifyMemo()` - Write permission check for memo modification

12. **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`** (Lines 173-250)
    - `batchConvertMemoRelations()` - Visibility filtering when loading memo relations (line 186)

13. **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go`** (Lines 306-312)
    - Visibility-aware notification delivery (checks if memo is private/protected)

14. **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go`** (Lines 67, 84)
    - Notification dispatch respects visibility constraints

### **Access Control Configuration**

15. **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go`** (Lines 11-84)
    - Defines public endpoints: `GetMemo`, `ListMemos`, `ListMemoComments`, `GetMemoByShare`
    - Other operations require authentication
    - Public methods still enforce visibility filtering in service layer (see comment line 32)

### **Visibility Enforcement Patterns**

The codebase uses two primary patterns:
1. **Direct visibility checks** on `memo.Visibility` field (comparing against `store.Public`, `store.Private`, `store.Protected`)
2. **Filter-based visibility** using `memoFind.VisibilityList` and filter expressions like `creator_id == X || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]`

All memo visibility enforcement ultimately flows through these central points and respects the visibility model: **PRIVATE** (creator only), **PROTECTED** (creator + authenticated users), **PUBLIC** (everyone).</result>
